questions.title: The pudendal (Alcock's) canal in the ischioanal fossa carries the inferior rectal vessels and nerve
questions.question: Which of the following is a content of the pudendal (Alcock's) canal, formed within the lateral wall of the ischioanal (ischiorectal) fossa?
questions.subject: androl

explanations.A: Correct. The pudendal (Alcock's) canal is a fascial tunnel in the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa, carrying the internal pudendal vessels and pudendal nerve toward the perineum. Within its course the inferior rectal (anal) artery and nerve branch off and cross the ischioanal fossa to supply the anal canal and external anal sphincter. This is why the inferior rectal vessels/nerve are classically listed as contents encountered in relation to this canal.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The obturator nerve runs in the pelvis and through the obturator canal in the obturator membrane, not through the pudendal canal in the ischioanal fossa.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen and runs posterior to the ischioanal fossa in the gluteal region; it is not a content of the pudendal canal.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The superior rectal artery is the continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery supplying the upper rectum from above; it does not run through the pudendal canal, which lies below the pelvic floor in the perineum.

questions.learning_objective: State that the pudendal (Alcock's) canal, in the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa, carries the internal pudendal vessels and pudendal nerve, from which the inferior rectal artery and nerve branch to cross the fossa.

questions.title: The unregressed cranial end of the male paramesonephric duct forms the appendix of the testis
questions.question: In the male fetus, Sertoli-cell MIH causes regression of most of the paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct, but its unregressed cranial (upper) end persists as which vestigial structure?
questions.subject: androl

explanations.A: Correct. Müllerian-inhibiting hormone (MIH/AMH) from fetal Sertoli cells causes regression of almost the entire paramesonephric duct in the male. Its cranial-most tip, however, is spared. That unregressed tip persists as a small vestigial appendage attached to the upper pole of the testis, the appendix of the testis (hydatid of Morgagni).
explanations.B: Incorrect. The appendix of the epididymis is a mesonephric (Wolffian) duct remnant, not a paramesonephric duct remnant — it arises from an unincorporated cranial mesonephric tubule/duct segment near the head of the epididymis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The prostatic utricle is the remnant of the fused caudal ends of the paired paramesonephric ducts (the male homologue of the uterus/upper vagina), opening on the seminal colliculus — a caudal, not cranial, paramesonephric remnant.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The paradidymis is a cluster of vestigial mesonephric tubules near the spermatic cord, not a paramesonephric duct derivative.

questions.learning_objective: State that the unregressed cranial (upper) end of the paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct persists in the male as the appendix of the testis.

questions.title: Breast cancer in the upper outer quadrant classically spreads first to the anterior (pectoral) axillary nodes
questions.question: A female patient has a breast carcinoma located in the left upper outer quadrant. Which group of lymph nodes is most likely to be involved first?
questions.subject: gyn

explanations.A: Correct. Roughly three-quarters of breast lymph drains along vessels that follow the lateral thoracic vessels to the anterior (pectoral) group of axillary nodes, which lie along the lower border of pectoralis minor. The upper outer quadrant — the quadrant with the greatest breast tissue volume — drains predominantly through this route, making the pectoral axillary nodes the first-echelon (sentinel) nodes most often involved.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The parasternal (internal thoracic) nodes chiefly drain the medial breast quadrants, not the upper outer quadrant, following lymphatics that accompany the internal thoracic vessels through the intercostal spaces.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Supraclavicular nodes are a later echelon, typically involved only after the axillary nodes, once disease has progressed beyond the first-tier nodal groups — they are not the first nodes involved from an upper outer quadrant tumor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The posterior (subscapular) axillary group drains lymph chiefly from the back and posterior shoulder region via the subscapular vessels, not primarily from the breast.

questions.learning_objective: State that the upper outer quadrant of the breast, which contains the greatest volume of breast tissue, drains predominantly to the anterior (pectoral) group of axillary lymph nodes.

questions.title: Primitive sex cords become histologically recognizable in the gonadal ridge by about the 7th week
questions.question: By approximately which week of gestation do primitive (primary) sex cords become histologically recognizable within the developing gonadal (genital) ridge?
questions.subject: androl

explanations.A: Correct. Primordial germ cells arrive in the genital ridges by about the 5th–6th week. The surrounding coelomic epithelium then proliferates to form primary (primitive) sex cords that become histologically identifiable within the indifferent gonad by about the 7th week. From that point, testis- or ovary-determining genes drive further sex-specific differentiation of these cords.
explanations.B: Incorrect. At the 4th week the genital (gonadal) ridge itself is only just beginning to form as a thickening of the intermediate mesoderm/coelomic epithelium; it is too early for organized sex cords to have formed.
explanations.C: Incorrect. By the 5th week, primordial germ cells are still migrating into the genital ridge; the ridge is still an undifferentiated (indifferent) structure without organized, histologically distinct sex cords.
explanations.D: Incorrect. By the 10th week, the gonad has already committed to a testis or ovary phenotype with well-developed structures (seminiferous cords with Sertoli cells, or primary follicles); this is well beyond the initial appearance of primitive sex cords.

questions.learning_objective: State that primitive (primary) sex cords become histologically recognizable within the indifferent gonadal ridge by about the 7th week of gestation.

questions.title: Degarelix, a GnRH receptor antagonist, causes an immediate fall in gonadotropin secretion without an initial flare
questions.question: Regarding degarelix, which of the following statements is true?
questions.subject: pharm

options.A: As a GnRH receptor antagonist, it immediately and directly reduces gonadotropin (LH/FSH) secretion, without an initial testosterone flare
options.B: It produces an initial testosterone flare before suppression, as GnRH agonists such as leuprolide do
options.C: It stimulates gonadotropin secretion by mimicking the pulsatile action of natural GnRH
options.D: It has no effect on gonadotropin secretion and instead acts as a direct androgen receptor antagonist

explanations.A: Correct. Degarelix is a GnRH receptor antagonist: it competitively blocks pituitary GnRH receptors immediately, without the initial receptor stimulation that agonists produce, so gonadotropin (LH and FSH) secretion — and downstream testicular testosterone production — falls rapidly from the first dose, with no testosterone flare. This makes it useful in advanced prostate cancer when an agonist-induced flare (which can worsen bone pain or cause spinal cord compression) must be avoided.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An initial testosterone flare is characteristic of GnRH agonists (e.g., leuprolide, goserelin), which transiently overstimulate the pituitary before receptor downregulation suppresses gonadotropins; degarelix, as an antagonist, produces no such flare.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Degarelix blocks, rather than mimics, GnRH receptor activation; it does not stimulate gonadotropin secretion at any point in its action.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Degarelix acts centrally at the pituitary GnRH receptor to suppress gonadotropin secretion; it is not a peripheral androgen receptor antagonist (that mechanism instead describes drugs such as flutamide or bicalutamide).

questions.learning_objective: State that degarelix is a GnRH receptor antagonist that immediately suppresses gonadotropin (LH/FSH) secretion and testosterone production, without the initial testosterone flare seen with GnRH agonists.

questions.title: Stereocilia lining the ductus (vas) deferens increase luminal surface area and help move sperm along the duct
questions.question: What is the function of the stereocilia lining the epithelium of the ductus (vas) deferens?
questions.subject: androl

options.A: They are long, non-motile microvilli that increase the epithelial surface area, aiding fluid absorption and the onward movement of spermatozoa along the duct
options.B: They beat rhythmically to actively propel sperm forward, similar to the motile cilia of the respiratory tract
options.C: They are the principal secretory source of seminal plasma proteins
options.D: They actively phagocytose and remove defective or degenerating spermatozoa from the lumen

explanations.A: Correct. Despite their name, stereocilia are not true motile cilia but long, branching, non-motile microvilli. By greatly increasing the apical surface area of the pseudostratified columnar epithelium lining the epididymis and ductus deferens, they support reabsorption of the bulk of the luminal testicular fluid and, by concentrating and directing the residual luminal flow, are classically credited with assisting the passage of spermatozoa along the duct toward ejaculation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Stereocilia lack the axonemal (9+2 microtubule) structure and motor proteins required for active beating; true motile cilia with that structure are instead found in tissues such as the respiratory epithelium and the uterine tube.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bulk secretion of seminal plasma proteins is chiefly a function of the seminal vesicles and prostate gland, not the stereocilia of the ductus deferens.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Phagocytosis of defective sperm and residual bodies is a recognized epididymal epithelial function but is carried out by the principal cells generally, not specifically attributed to the stereocilia themselves.

questions.learning_objective: State that the stereocilia lining the epididymis and ductus (vas) deferens are non-motile, long microvilli that increase epithelial surface area for fluid absorption and assist the onward movement of spermatozoa along the duct.

questions.title: hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast maintains the corpus luteum's progesterone secretion in early pregnancy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the corpus luteum of pregnancy is true?
questions.subject: obs

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin, secreted by the syncytiotrophoblast, maintains the corpus luteum's progesterone secretion until the placenta takes over steroidogenesis
options.B: The syncytiotrophoblast itself directly synthesizes progesterone from cholesterol, entirely independent of the corpus luteum
options.C: The corpus luteum degenerates immediately after fertilization regardless of hCG levels
options.D: Progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum suppresses hCG secretion through negative feedback on the syncytiotrophoblast

explanations.A: Correct. Once implantation occurs, the syncytiotrophoblast begins secreting human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), an LH-like hormone that binds LH/hCG receptors on the corpus luteum, rescuing it from the involution ('luteolysis') it would otherwise undergo and maintaining its progesterone (and estrogen) output. This corpus luteum of pregnancy sustains the endometrium until around 8–10 weeks, by which time the placenta itself has taken over adequate steroidogenesis (the 'luteal-placental shift').
explanations.B: Incorrect. In early pregnancy the placenta cannot independently complete progesterone synthesis without maternal cholesterol substrate and, before the luteal-placental shift, relies on the corpus luteum (which the syncytiotrophoblast's hCG maintains) rather than synthesizing progesterone entirely on its own from the outset.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Without hCG rescue, the corpus luteum would indeed regress around the time of the expected menses, but hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast actively prevents this regression in a successful pregnancy, maintaining it as the corpus luteum of pregnancy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The relationship described is reversed: hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast supports the corpus luteum's progesterone secretion, rather than progesterone suppressing hCG output.

questions.learning_objective: State that human chorionic gonadotropin, secreted by the syncytiotrophoblast, rescues and maintains the corpus luteum's progesterone secretion in early pregnancy until the placenta assumes steroidogenesis.

questions.title: Exclusive breastfeeding suppresses GnRH pulsatility, producing lactational amenorrhea for up to about 6 months
questions.question: Regarding lactation in an exclusively breastfeeding mother, which of the following statements is true?
questions.subject: gyn

options.A: Frequent, exclusive breastfeeding elevates prolactin, which suppresses pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH secretion, producing amenorrhea for up to about 6 months postpartum
options.B: Normal ovulatory menstrual cycles resume within about 2 weeks of delivery regardless of breastfeeding frequency
options.C: Prolactin has no meaningful effect on the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis during lactation
options.D: Breastfeeding stimulates, rather than suppresses, pulsatile GnRH secretion, accelerating the return of ovulation

explanations.A: Correct. Frequent suckling stimulates sustained prolactin release, and high prolactin levels suppress hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility (partly via increased hypothalamic dopaminergic/opioid tone), which in turn lowers pituitary LH and FSH secretion and blocks ovulation. With frequent, exclusive breastfeeding (including night feeds, with no significant supplementation), this can reliably suppress fertility and menstruation for up to about 6 months postpartum — the basis of the lactational amenorrhea method of contraception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. With frequent exclusive breastfeeding, ovulation and menses are typically suppressed for months, not resumed within 2 weeks; return of fertility is much faster in mothers who are not breastfeeding or who breastfeed infrequently/with supplementation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Prolactin has a well-established suppressive effect on the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis during lactation, which is precisely the mechanism underlying lactational amenorrhea.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The direction of the effect is reversed: prolactin released during frequent breastfeeding suppresses, rather than stimulates, pulsatile GnRH secretion.

questions.learning_objective: State that frequent, exclusive breastfeeding raises prolactin, which suppresses pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH secretion and can produce lactational amenorrhea for up to about 6 months postpartum.

questions.title: Placental estrogen rises sharply in the final weeks of pregnancy, raising myometrial excitability before parturition
questions.question: Which hormonal change is characteristically expected during the final weeks of pregnancy, in the lead-up to parturition?
questions.subject: obs

options.A: A sharp, accelerating rise in placental estrogen secretion, which increases myometrial excitability and oxytocin receptor expression
options.B: A sharp rise in progesterone relative to estrogen, reinforcing uterine quiescence right up to labor onset
options.C: A steady decline in both estrogen and progesterone output from mid-pregnancy onward
options.D: No significant change in placental estrogen output as term approaches

explanations.A: Correct. Placental estrogen output rises progressively through pregnancy and increases especially sharply in the final weeks before labor. This rising estrogen increases myometrial gap-junction formation, oxytocin receptor density, and overall uterine excitability, helping shift the uterus from the quiescent state of most of pregnancy toward the coordinated contractility needed for labor.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Late pregnancy is instead characterized by a relative shift toward estrogen dominance (a fall in the progesterone:estrogen ratio at the myometrium), not a further rise in progesterone's relative influence, since progesterone is what maintains uterine quiescence and its withdrawal/functional decline favors labor onset.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Estrogen output rises, rather than declines, as term approaches; a decline in both hormones is not the characteristic pre-labor pattern.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Estrogen output changes substantially — rising sharply — rather than remaining static, in the weeks leading up to parturition.

questions.learning_objective: State that placental estrogen secretion rises sharply in the final weeks of pregnancy, increasing myometrial excitability and oxytocin receptor expression ahead of parturition.

questions.title: Full-thickness squamous atypia without maturation and an intact basement membrane defines cervical HSIL (CIN 3)
questions.question: A female patient is evaluated for an abnormal Pap smear. A cervical biopsy shows atypical squamous cells throughout the entire thickness of the epithelium, with no evidence of epithelial maturation; the basement membrane appears intact. What is the appropriate diagnosis?
questions.subject: gyn

options.A: Cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL / CIN 3)
options.B: Cervical low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL / CIN 1)
options.C: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix
options.D: Microinvasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix

explanations.A: Correct. Full-thickness replacement of the squamous epithelium by atypical, immature basaloid cells, with no surface maturation, defines high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). This corresponds to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3), or carcinoma in situ. Because the basement membrane remains intact, the lesion stays confined above it rather than becoming invasive.
explanations.B: Incorrect. LSIL (CIN 1) shows atypia and koilocytic change confined to the lower third of the epithelium, with normal maturation preserved in the upper two-thirds — not the full-thickness atypia described here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Invasive squamous cell carcinoma requires malignant cells to breach the basement membrane and infiltrate the underlying stroma; the stem explicitly states the basement membrane appears intact, arguing against invasion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Microinvasive carcinoma implies limited, measurable stromal invasion beyond the basement membrane, which is again inconsistent with an intact basement membrane on this biopsy.

questions.learning_objective: State that full-thickness squamous epithelial atypia without maturation, with an intact basement membrane, defines cervical HSIL (CIN 3).

questions.title: Papillary serous carcinoma is the most aggressive histologic type of endometrial carcinoma
questions.question: Which of the following is the most aggressive histologic type of endometrial carcinoma?
questions.subject: gyn

explanations.A: Correct. Papillary serous carcinoma is a type II endometrial carcinoma, typically arising in an atrophic (not hyperplastic) endometrium in older, often thinner postmenopausal women, frequently harboring TP53 mutations. It behaves aggressively even when confined to a small volume of tissue, spreads early via peritoneal (transtubal) dissemination in a pattern resembling ovarian serous carcinoma, and carries the worst prognosis among the endometrial carcinoma subtypes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Endometrioid adenocarcinoma is the most common type (type I), classically estrogen-driven and arising in a background of endometrial hyperplasia; it is generally lower-grade and carries a substantially better prognosis than serous carcinoma.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mucinous carcinoma is an uncommon, generally well-differentiated variant of endometrioid-type carcinoma with a comparatively favorable prognosis, not the most aggressive subtype.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Clear cell carcinoma is also a type II carcinoma with an aggressive course and poor prognosis, but standard teaching ranks papillary serous carcinoma as the single most aggressive and worst-prognosis endometrial carcinoma subtype overall.

questions.learning_objective: State that papillary serous carcinoma is the most aggressive histologic subtype of endometrial carcinoma, classified as a type II (non-estrogen-driven) tumor with early peritoneal spread and a poor prognosis.

questions.title: Choriocarcinoma lacks chorionic villi and their fibrovascular stroma
questions.question: Choriocarcinoma is characteristically composed of all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.subject: obs

options.A: Chorionic villi with their fibrovascular stroma
options.D: Extensive areas of hemorrhage and necrosis

explanations.A: Correct. A defining histologic feature of choriocarcinoma is the complete absence of chorionic villi. The tumor is instead composed purely of a biphasic proliferation of cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast, without any villous fibrovascular stroma. This absence of villi distinguishes it from a hydatidiform mole, which does show abnormal, often hydropic, villi.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sheets/islands of cytotrophoblast cells ARE a characteristic component of choriocarcinoma, forming part of the biphasic cyto- and syncytiotrophoblastic proliferation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Syncytiotrophoblast, the multinucleated, hCG-secreting component, IS a characteristic component of choriocarcinoma and is in fact the source of the markedly elevated beta-hCG used to monitor the disease.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Extensive hemorrhage and necrosis ARE characteristic of choriocarcinoma, reflecting its highly vascular, rapidly proliferative and locally destructive growth pattern with early hematogenous spread.

questions.learning_objective: State that choriocarcinoma is a biphasic proliferation of cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast with extensive hemorrhage and necrosis, but — unlike a hydatidiform mole — it characteristically lacks chorionic villi.

questions.title: Peau d'orange of the breast skin results from infiltration of the dermal lymphatics by tumor
questions.question: The peau d'orange (orange-peel) appearance of the mammary skin, seen in some cases of breast carcinoma, is due to:
questions.subject: gyn

options.A: Infiltration of the dermal lymphatics by tumor, causing lymphedema and skin pitting at the fixed hair follicles
options.B: Direct invasion of the epidermis by malignant tumor cells
options.C: Chronic inflammatory dermal edema unrelated to any underlying malignancy
options.D: Shortening of Cooper's ligaments producing focal skin dimpling and retraction

explanations.A: Correct. Peau d'orange results when tumor emboli obstruct the dermal lymphatic channels of the breast skin, causing localized lymphedema. Because the skin remains tethered to the underlying dermis at the sites of hair follicles while the surrounding edematous skin swells, the surface takes on a pitted, orange-peel texture — a classic sign of locally advanced or inflammatory breast carcinoma.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Peau d'orange is a lymphatic obstruction phenomenon in the dermis, not the result of tumor cells directly invading/replacing the epidermis itself, though advanced disease can eventually also involve the skin directly.
explanations.C: Incorrect. While it manifests as dermal edema, peau d'orange in this clinical context specifically reflects tumor-caused dermal lymphatic obstruction, not an unrelated inflammatory process.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Skin dimpling/retraction from shortened, tumor-tethered Cooper's (suspensory) ligaments is a separate, distinct physical sign from peau d'orange, which instead reflects dermal lymphatic obstruction and edema rather than ligamentous traction.

questions.learning_objective: State that peau d'orange of the breast skin is produced by tumor infiltration of the dermal lymphatics, causing localized lymphedema with skin pitting at follicle attachment points.

questions.title: HPV types 16 and 18 are implicated in penile squamous cell carcinoma
questions.question: Infection with high-risk human papillomavirus types 16 and 18 is most strongly implicated in the pathogenesis of which penile malignancy?
questions.subject: androl

options.C: Basal cell carcinoma of the penis

explanations.A: Correct. High-risk HPV types, chiefly 16 and 18, are detected in a substantial proportion of penile squamous cell carcinomas. They are considered a major etiologic factor, alongside other risk factors such as lack of circumcision, phimosis, chronic balanitis and smoking. HPV-driven tumors typically arise via a precursor penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN), analogous to cervical HSIL/CIN.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Penile melanoma arises from melanocytes and is not an HPV-associated malignancy; its pathogenesis relates to melanocytic transformation rather than viral oncogenesis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Basal cell carcinoma of the penis is rare and, unlike cutaneous BCC elsewhere linked to UV exposure, is not characteristically an HPV-driven tumor in the way squamous cell carcinoma is.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Kaposi sarcoma is caused by human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8), not HPV, and arises from lymphatic endothelial cells rather than squamous epithelium.

questions.learning_objective: State that high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 are strongly implicated in the pathogenesis of penile squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.title: Tumbling motility on wet mount is characteristic of Listeria monocytogenes
questions.question: A characteristic 'tumbling' motility pattern on wet-mount microscopy at room temperature is most typical of which organism?
questions.subject: inf

explanations.A: Correct. Listeria monocytogenes is a motile, flagellated gram-positive rod that shows a characteristic tumbling, end-over-end motility on wet-mount microscopy when grown at room temperature (20–25°C). Flagellar expression is temperature-regulated and is markedly reduced at 37°C, so this feature is best seen at room temperature. It is a classic identifying feature distinguishing Listeria from morphologically similar gram-positive rods.
explanations.B: Incorrect. E. coli is motile via peritrichous flagella producing smooth, directional swimming, not the distinctive tumbling pattern attributed to Listeria.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Staphylococcus aureus is a non-motile gram-positive coccus arranged in clusters; it lacks flagella entirely.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Unlike most other Clostridium species, Clostridium perfringens is characteristically non-motile despite being a gram-positive rod, so it would not display any tumbling motility.

questions.learning_objective: State that listeria monocytogenes shows a characteristic tumbling motility pattern on wet-mount microscopy at room temperature, a key identifying laboratory feature.

questions.title: Low birth weight, microcephaly and cataract in a neonate suggest congenital rubella syndrome
questions.question: A neonate presents with low birth weight, microcephaly, and congenital cataract. Which congenital infection is most consistent with this presentation?
questions.subject: inf

explanations.A: Correct. Congenital rubella syndrome classically produces the triad of sensorineural deafness, congenital cataract (and other eye defects), and cardiac malformations such as patent ductus arteriosus. It is also typically accompanied by growth restriction (low birth weight) and microcephaly. These findings reflect first-trimester maternal rubella infection, during the critical period of fetal organogenesis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Congenital toxoplasmosis classically produces the triad of chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial (diffuse) calcifications, rather than congenital cataract as its hallmark ocular finding.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Congenital CMV more typically causes periventricular intracranial calcifications, sensorineural hearing loss, hepatosplenomegaly, petechiae ('blueberry muffin' rash) and microcephaly, but cataract is not its characteristic ocular hallmark the way it is for rubella.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Congenital syphilis classically presents with findings such as saddle nose, saber shins, Hutchinson teeth, and rhagades, rather than the cataract–deafness–cardiac triad specific to congenital rubella.

questions.learning_objective: State that congenital rubella syndrome classically presents with congenital cataract, sensorineural deafness, cardiac malformations, microcephaly and low birth weight, following maternal rubella infection, especially in the first trimester.

questions.title: Oral contraceptive pill use is a recognized predisposing factor for symptomatic Trichomonas vaginalis infection
questions.question: Which of the following is a recognized predisposing factor that increases the risk of symptomatic Trichomonas vaginalis vaginitis?
questions.subject: gyn

options.A: Use of oral contraceptive pills, which alter vaginal pH and glycogen content favorably for the organism
options.C: Strict vaginal hygiene practices, including regular douching
options.D: A low vaginal pH maintained by a healthy, lactobacillus-dominant flora

explanations.A: Correct. Trichomonas vaginalis thrives best in an environment with an elevated vaginal pH and an altered glycogen/estrogen milieu. Recognized predisposing factors include use of oral contraceptive pills, pregnancy, and disruption of the normal lactobacillus-dominant flora, for example from antibiotic use. All of these favor the organism's growth and symptomatic infection.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Trichomoniasis is most common in sexually active reproductive-age women, not specifically linked to postmenopausal atrophic mucosa as its classic predisposing state.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vaginal douching disrupts protective lactobacillus flora and is a recognized risk factor for various vaginal infections, but it is not the answer being tested here as the paired predisposing factor for T. vaginalis in this item; more importantly, it works by disrupting protective flora rather than the mechanism attributed to OCPs (pH/glycogen alteration).
explanations.D: Incorrect. A healthy lactobacillus-dominant flora maintaining a low vaginal pH is protective against T. vaginalis and other vaginal pathogens, not a predisposing factor for infection.
